Almohad Caliphate was a North African empire ruled by a Berber Muslim dynasty in the 12th and 13th centuries that lasted from 1121-1269.
This Malaysian politician became his country's 10th prime minister in 2022 and promptly appointed himself finance minister as well — who is he?

Book of Numbers (from Greek, Arithmoi, lit. 'numbers') is the fourth book of the Hebrew Bible and the fourth of five books of the Jewish Torah.

This Belgian politician became his country's youngest development minister at age 31, later led a liberal party, served as prime minister, and then presided over the European Council from 2019 to 2024. Who is he?
Charles Michel (born 21 December 1975) is a Belgian politician who served as the president of the European Council from 2019 to 2024.
This Taiwanese businesswoman and former Merrill Lynch analyst became a Legislative Yuan member in 2022 and ran as Ko Wen-je's vice-presidential pick in Taiwan's 2024 election — who is she?
Cynthia Wu (pinyin: W Xnyng; Wade-; born 18 May 1978) is a Taiwanese businesswoman, politician, and former financial analyst.

Domingo Faustino Sarmiento (15 February 1811 - 11 September 1888) was President of Argentina from 1868 to 1874.
This American murderer served as a hitman for his uncle's crime ring during a string of Osage Nation killings, and was ultimately pardoned by Oklahoma's governor in 1966. Who is he?
Ernest Burkhart (September 11, 1892 - December 1, 1986) was an American murderer who participated in the Osage Indian murders as a hitman for his uncle William King Hale's crime ring.
This Haitian leader trained as a doctor fighting tropical disease before becoming president in 1957 and turning his rule increasingly autocratic — who is he?
François Duvalier (14 April 1907 - 21 April 1971), also known as Papa Doc, was a Haitian politician and physician who served as president of Haiti from 1957 until his death in 1971.

In November 1688 the Catholic King James II was deposed in favor of his daughter Mary II and her Dutch husband William of Orange — an event some historians call the last successful invasion of England. What is it called?

Glorious Revolution was the deposition of King James II in November 1688. The two ruled as joint monarchs of England, Scotland, and Ireland until Mary's death in 1694, when William became ruler in his own right.
Born and raised in New York, this politician moved to San Francisco in 1972, opened a camera store, and became the first openly gay man elected to public office in California — who is he?

Harvey Milk (May 22, 1930 - November 27, 1978) was an American politician and the first openly gay man to be elected to public office in California, as a member of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors.
A former Air Force commander, this leader stepped into Egypt's presidency after Anwar Sadat's 1981 assassination and held it for nearly thirty years until a revolution forced him out. Who was he?

Hosni Mubarak (4 May 1928 - 25 February 2020) was an Egyptian politician and military officer who served as the 4th president of Egypt from 1981 until his resignation in 2011, following the Egyptian revolution.
The only queen to reign in her own right over a unified Spain, this monarch took the throne a month before her third birthday in 1833 and was deposed in 1868 — who was she?
Isabella II (10 October 1830 - 9 April 1904) was Queen of Spain from 1833 until her deposition in 1868.
Nicknamed the Milwaukee Cannibal, this American serial killer murdered seventeen men and boys between 1978 and 1991, luring many victims to his Wisconsin apartment — who was he?

Jeffrey Dahmer (May 21, 1960 - November 28, 1994), also known as the Milwaukee Cannibal or the Milwaukee Monster, was an American serial killer and sex offender who killed and dismembered seventeen men and boys between 1978 and 1991.
This Spanish PSOE leader left office in December 2011 after pursuing peace talks with ETA and pushing through reforms to the country's autonomous statutes — who is he?
José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero (born 4 August 1960) is a Spanish politician and member of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE).
This Tamil and Telugu film star, now a politician, has taken home a Kalaimamani Award and a Kerala State Film Award across a 200-plus-film career — who is she?
Khushbu Sundar (born Nakhat Khan on 29 September 1970) is an Indian politician, actress, film producer and television personality.
The only president of Ukraine ever to serve two full terms, his 1994-to-2005 presidency brought economic stabilization but also scandal and the rise of powerful oligarchs — who was he?
Leonid Kuchma (born 9 August 1938) is a Ukrainian politician who served as the second president of Ukraine from 19 July 1994 to 23 January 2005.
At its greatest extent, this Javanese Hindu-Buddhist maritime empire's territory and tributary states spanned nearly the entire Indonesian archipelago — what's the historic empire?

Majapahit (Javanese) or (western dialect)), also known as Wilwatikta (Javanese), was a Javanese Hindu-Buddhist thalassocratic empire in Southeast Asia based on the island of Java (in modern-day Indonesia).

First elected to the Reichstag in 1903, this Centre Party politician turned against unrestricted submarine warfare and proposed a 1917 peace resolution before heading Germany's armistice delegation — who is he?
Matthias Erzberger (20 September 1875 - 26 August 1921) was a German Centre Party politician who served as the minister of finance of Germany from 1919 to 1920.

Born in 1942, this Republican has held the Senate seat from Kentucky since 1985 and was the longest-serving senator in the state's history. He served as Senate Republican leader for 18 years across three stints. Who is he?
Mitch McConnell (m-; born February 20, 1942) is an American Republican Party politician and attorney serving as the senior United States senator from Kentucky, a seat he has held since 1985.
This Salvadoran leader ran an advertising company before entering politics, served as mayor of San Salvador, and founded the Nuevas Ideas party after being ousted from the FMLN — who is he?
Nayib Bukele (born 24 July 1981) is a Salvadoran politician and businessman who has served as the 43rd president of El Salvador since 2019.
This Swedish politician led the Social Democratic Party and served as Prime Minister twice — 1969 to 1976, then 1982 until his assassination in 1986. Who was this Stockholm statesman?
Olof Palme (30 January 1927 - 28 February 1986) was a Swedish politician and statesman who served as Prime Minister of Sweden from 1969 to 1976 and 1982 to 1986.

A printer and War of 1812 militia lieutenant, this Whig was twice elected mayor of Washington D.C. while amassing one of the most extensive private collections of Revolution-era maps and manuscripts in America — who?

Built on the belief that inherited attributes make one group superior to another, this term also covers everyday prejudice against people of a different ethnic background. What is it?
Racism is the belief that groups of humans possess different behavioral traits corresponding to inherited attributes and can be divided based on the superiority of one race or ethnicity over another.
The eldest son of a US president, and the only one of his four siblings to live past 18, this lawyer served as Secretary of War and later as US Ambassador to Great Britain. Who was he?
Robert Todd Lincoln (August 1, 1843 - July 26, 1926) was an American lawyer and businessman.

Originally referring to inhabitants of ancient Arabia Petraea, this medieval European term evolved after the rise of Islam to become the standard Christian label for Muslims and the Muslim world broadly — what's the term?
Saracen was commonly used in medieval Europe to refer to a person who lived in or near what the ancient Romans knew as Arabia Petraea and Arabia Deserta.

With backing from the U.S. and Belgium, this military chief of staff deposed Congo's first democratically elected government in 1960 and later ruled the renamed nation of Zaire for over two decades — who was he?
Mobutu Sese Seko: President of DR Congo and Zaire from 1965 to 1997.

Muslim Brotherhood: Transnational Sunni Islamist organization.

Second Sino-Japanese War: 1937–1945 conflict in East Asia. It is often regarded as the beginning of World War II in Asia, as the wars became heavily intertwined after Japan's entry into World War II.

Shiva: Major deity in Hinduism. Shiva is one of the five equivalent deities in Panchayatana puja of the Smarta tradition of Hinduism.
A Thracian gladiator born near the Strymon river, this figure led an escaped-slave uprising against the Roman Republic known as the Third Servile War — who was he?
Spartacus: Thracian gladiator who led a slave revolt. Spartacus is described to be born near the Strymon river, in Thrace (now known as Bulgaria), possibly from the Maedi tribe.

Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Archimedes is a mathematician. Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
What is the atomic number of Radium?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
What is the atomic number of Zinc?
Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
In what year did Stephen Hawking die?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Theobroma cacao discovered?
Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Mikoyan MiG-31: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-31 is the fastest known operational combat aircraft, with a top speed around 3,000 km/h (1,600 knots).
Which company manufactures CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Triangulum Australe?
Triangulum Australe: Américo Vespucio. Triangulum Australe is a small constellation in the far Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Ichthyosaurus?
Ichthyosaurus: Mary Anning. It is among the best known ichthyosaur genera, as it is the type genus of the order Ichthyosauria.
Who is credited with discovering Theobroma cacao?
Theobroma cacao: Christopher Columbus. Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Who is credited with discovering Krypton?
Krypton: William Ramsay. Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

First coined as a term in 1852, this pattern of continued drinking despite its harms affected an estimated 283 million people worldwide as of 2016, according to the World Health Organization — name the condition?
Alcoholism is the continued drinking of alcohol despite the problems it causes.
This order of ray-finned fish is named for a modified fin ray that dangles like bait to lure in prey, much like a human with a fishing rod — what are they called?

Anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes. The majority are bottom-dwellers, being demersal fish, while the aberrant deep-sea anglerfish are pelagic, (mostly) living high in the water column.

This English science fiction writer, futurist, and undersea explorer received the 1961 Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science, across a career spanning novels, essays, and television hosting — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke (16 December 1917 - 19 March 2008) was an English science fiction writer, science writer, futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and television series host.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary one-sided facial paralysis of unknown cause can droop an eyebrow, alter taste, and make sounds painfully loud — what is it?
Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
Element 107, a synthetic transactinide whose most stable known isotope lasts barely 2.4 minutes, takes its name from a famous Danish physicist — what is it?
Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Unlike ordinary weight loss from undereating, this illness-linked syndrome strips away muscle mass in ways good nutrition can't fully undo — what condition is it?
Cachexia is a syndrome that occurs in people with certain illnesses, causing muscle loss that cannot be fully reversed with improved nutrition.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine and fifty percent bound to plasma proteins in your bloodstream, what class of neurotransmitter has a benzene ring topped with two hydroxyl groups plus a side-chain amine?

Catecholamine (abbreviated CA), most typically a 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine, is a monoamine neurotransmitter, an organic compound that has a catechol (benzene with two hydroxyl side groups next to each other) and a side-chain amine.
Grown for blue-flowered roadside roots that become a coffee substitute, or for bitter salad leaves like escarole and radicchio, which plant genus covers both chicory and endive?
Cichorium is a genus of plants in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae.
This common bowel condition causes hard, dry stools passed fewer than three times a week, sometimes leading to hemorrhoids or fissures — what is it?
Constipation is a bowel dysfunction that makes bowel movements infrequent or hard to pass.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded a company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998, then went on to co-found and lead a massively popular online gaming and creation platform — who is he?
David Baszucki (buh-; born January 20, 1963) is a Canadian-born American entrepreneur, engineer, and software developer.
First proposed as a model organism in 1901, this tiny insect species has become biology's workhorse for genetics research, and it's the one buzzing around your rotting fruit bowl. Name the species?
Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fly (an insect of the order Diptera) in the family Drosophilidae.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.

This synthetic opioid is 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine and is now notorious in emergency medicine. Initially developed as a pain medication for cancer patients and post-surgical recovery, it works by activating opioid receptors — what is this drug?
Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'milky,' this term names any gravity-bound system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter, ranging from tiny dwarfs to supergiants with a hundred trillion stars. What is it?
Galaxy is a system of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Known as 'The Last Universalist' for mastering nearly every branch of his field, this French mathematician and physicist founded modern chaos theory through his study of the three-body problem — who is he?
Henri Poincaré (29 April 1854 - 17 July 1912) was a French mathematician, theoretical physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science.
A body-temperature emergency defined as a reading above 104°F, this condition kills roughly half a million people annually and is most commonly triggered by heat stroke — what is it called?
Hyperthermia is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.

From deep-sea gribbles to the woodlice under your garden stones, members of this crustacean order share seven pairs of jointed limbs and brood their young in a pouch called a marsupium — what is the order?
Isopoda is an order of crustaceans. The order is divided into eleven suborders.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
This genus of deciduous conifers, unusual for shedding its needles each year, dominates the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada, making it the most abundant tree genus on Earth — what is it called?
Larch are deciduous conifers in the genus Larix, of the family Pinaceae.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (symbol Lv, number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — named for a California national laboratory. Which element is it?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Sometimes nicknamed 'sea cows,' these large, fully aquatic herbivorous marine mammals can grow up to 13 feet long and include Amazonian, West Indian, and West African species — what are they called?
Manatee (family Trichechidae, genus Trichechus) are large, fully aquatic, mostly herbivorous marine mammals sometimes known as sea cows.
Its three main jobs are converting food into usable energy, building macromolecules like proteins and lipids, and excreting waste — the chemistry that keeps every living thing alive. What is it?
Metabolism (from) refers to the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that occur within living organisms.
Named for the river near which its type fossil was found by a Dutch chalk quarry in the 18th century, this genus of marine reptile lived until the end of the Cretaceous — what is it?
Mosasaurus ("lizard of the Meuse River") is the type genus (defining example) of the Mosasauridae, an extinct group of aquatic squamate reptiles.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).

These pouched mammals originated in South America and crossed into the north during the Great American Interchange; one species is so common in the U.S. that people just call it a 'possum.' What is it?
Opossum are members of the marsupial order Didelphimorphia endemic to the Americas.
This New York Times columnist of 24 years was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel in economics for explaining the patterns of international trade and where economic activity clusters. Who is he?
Paul Krugman (born February 28, 1953) is an American economist who is the Distinguished Professor of Economics at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York.
Odorless when pure but reeking of rotting fish in technical grade, this colorless PH3 gas can burst into a luminous flame on contact with air — what highly toxic compound is it?
Phosphine (IUPAC name: phosphane) is a colorless, flammable, highly toxic compound with the chemical formula PH3, classed as a pnictogen hydride.
Though it looks like a small dolphin, this cetacean is actually more closely related to narwhals and belugas, and can be told apart by its flattened, spade-shaped teeth — what animal is it?
Porpoise are small dolphin-like cetaceans classified under the family Phocoenidae.
Its blossoms are a beloved symbol of early spring throughout East Asia, and its crunchy fruit is marketed globally as the Asian or nashi pear - which tree species?
Pyrus pyrifolia is a species of pear tree native to southern China and northern Indochina that has been introduced to Korea, Japan and other parts of the world.

A brilliant English anatomist who coined the word 'Dinosauria,' meaning roughly 'terrible reptile,' he accepted that evolution happened but was an outspoken critic of Darwin's account of it. Who was he?
Richard Owen (20 July 1804 - 18 December 1892) was an English biologist, comparative anatomist and palaeontologist.
Marked by hearing voices, disorganized thinking, and flat affect, this condition is diagnosed by observed behavior rather than any objective test — what is it?
Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized variously by hallucinations (typically, hearing voices), delusions, disorganized thinking or behavior, and flat or inappropriate affect.
Long, thin and transparent, this hydrozoan drifts through the ocean as a colony of specialized zooids that together handle feeding, floating and jet propulsion — what marine organism is this?
Siphonophore (from Ancient Greek (siphn), meaning "tube" and - (-phros), meaning "bearing") are cnidarian animals of the hydrozoan order Siphonophorae.

Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes' and 'kernel,' this genus of spherical, Gram-positive bacteria grows in grape-like clusters and can survive with or without oxygen — what's the genus called?
Staphylococcus (staphul), meaning "bunch of grapes", and (kkkos), meaning "kernel" or "Kermes", is a genus of Gram-positive bacteria in the family Staphylococcaceae from the order Bacillales.
Though some scientists place it in its own genus, Acrocodia, the Malayan species is usually still classified within this genus of tapir — name this genus?
Tapirus is a genus of tapir which contains the living tapir species.
This intensely itchy, contagious fungal skin infection produces a red, scaly rash with a curved border across the groin and buttocks, mostly in men — what is it?

Tinea cruris (TC), also known as jock itch, is a common type of contagious, superficial fungal infection of the groin and buttocks region, which occurs predominantly but not exclusively in men and in hot-humid climates.
This bodily fluid, produced by the kidneys to flush out urea and other waste, can also serve a second life as a nitrogen-rich fertilizer for soil — what is it?
Urine is the fluid excreted by the kidneys of vertebrates to clear the bloodstream of excess water and metabolic by-products including urea, uric acid, and creatinine.
Native to Eastern and Southern Africa, this large antelope genus includes two species — one black, one blue — whose lineages diverged roughly a million years ago — what animal is it?
Wildebeest (VIL-), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
This military pilot became his country's first astronaut when he flew to the International Space Station aboard a 2024 mission — who is he?
Alper Gezeravcı: Turkish fighter pilot and astronaut (born 1979)
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Also nicknamed the cross spider or diadem spider for the white markings on its back, this orb-weaver is native to Europe but was introduced to North America — what species is it?

Araneus diadematus: Species of spider. The spider species Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Named for the physicist who shared a 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie, this SI unit measures one radioactive decay event per second — which unit?
Becquerel: SI derived unit of radioactivity.
Despite its name, only the soles of this tawny, spotted feline's paws are actually dark — and at just 35 to 52 centimetres long, it ranks as Africa's smallest wild feline species — what animal is it?
Black-footed cat: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa.
Also known as warble flies or gadflies, the larvae of which insect family live as internal parasites in mammal flesh or gut, with one species routinely infesting humans?
Botfly: Parasitic insect. Dermatobia hominis is the only species of botfly known to parasitize humans routinely, though other species of flies cause myiasis in humans.
He piloted the Lunar Module Eagle in 1969 to become the second person to walk on the Moon, and after Jim Lovell's death in 2025 became the oldest living astronaut — who is he?
Tetravalent and able to form four covalent bonds, this element known since antiquity ranks as the fourth most abundant in the universe by mass — which one is it?
Carbon: Chemical element with atomic number 6 (C)

Greek for "head-feet," fishers nickname these inkfish for their ink-squirting trick; their arms are muscular hydrostats modified from the primitive molluscan foot. Which marine class includes the octopus, squid, and nautilus?
Cephalopod: Class of mollusks. The study of cephalopods is a branch of malacology known as teuthology.
This form of cancer that begins in the tubes carrying digestive fluid from the liver can cause yellowing skin, dark urine, and pale stools — what is it?
Cholangiocarcinoma: Cancer of the bile ducts.
Commonly called the tailbone, this bone is the vestigial remnant of a tail in humans and other tailless primates, sitting just below the sacrum — which bone?
Coccyx: Bone of the pelvis. In tailless primates (e.g. humans and other great apes) since Nacholapithecus (a Miocene hominoid), the coccyx is the remnant of a vestigial tail.
One of the few metals found in nature in directly usable metallic form, this soft, pinkish-orange element with symbol Cu prizes its high thermal and electrical conductivity — what is it?
Copper: Chemical element with atomic number 29 (Cu)
This medical sign turns the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes a bluish-purple hue when blood isn't carrying enough oxygen, and comes in central and peripheral forms — what is it called?
Cyanosis: Decreased oxygen in the blood. Cyanosis is apparent usually in the body tissues covered with thin skin, including the mucous membranes, lips, nail beds, and ear lobes.
This medical and surgical specialty treats everything from inflammatory conditions and cancers to hair loss, requiring about four years of training beyond medical school — what field is it?
Dermatology: Field of medicine dealing with the hair, nails, skin, and its diseases.
Developed as a 14-bed sleeper upgrade of an earlier airliner, which low-wing propeller monoplane cruised at 207 mph and reshaped air travel from the 1930s through World War II?
Douglas DC-3: Airliner and military transport aircraft family.

Carried out mainly at power plants, this process transforms heat from burning fuel or nuclear fission — or the motion of water and wind — into power used by homes and businesses. What is this process called?
Electricity generation: Process of generating electrical power.
He coined the term 'quantum entanglement' in 1935 and shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac for his work on atomic theory — who is he?

Native to a huge swath of Eurasia but declared a noxious species in New South Wales after damaging native fish, this predatory freshwater game fish is known locally in Australia as 'redfin' — which fish?
Found on the forelimbs of most tetrapods, these prehensile, often opposable digits give primates like humans their dexterity for grasping and fine movement — what are they called?
The largest region of the brain's cerebral hemispheres, this most-forward area contains the primary motor cortex and is separated from the parietal and temporal regions by two grooves — what is it?
Frontal lobe: Part of the brain. The most anterior ventral, orbital end of the frontal lobe is known as the frontal pole, which is one of the three so-called poles of the cerebrum.
Named from Greek words for 'old man' and 'healer,' this medical specialty focuses on preventing and treating disease in older adults with no fixed age cutoff — what is it called?
Geriatrics: Medical specialty that focuses on health care of elderly people.
This branch of discrete mathematics studies structures made of vertices connected by edges, modeling pairwise relationships between objects — what field is it?

Graph theory: Area of discrete mathematics. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.
The best-known of these rodents is the golden or Syrian species, though dwarf varieties like Campbell's and the Roborovski are popular too — what small pet is this?
Its name Greek for 'different wings,' this insect suborder of about 40,000 species is the group most consistently termed 'true bugs' within Hemiptera — which group is it?
Heteroptera: Suborder of true bugs. The name "Heteroptera" is used in two very different ways in modern classifications.
Also known as dihydrocodeinone, this semi-synthetic opioid is often combined with acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain and is sold alone as an extended-release drug called Zohydro ER — what is it?
Hydrocodone: Opioid drug used in pain relief.
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length has been pegged to exactly 25.4 millimeters since the mid-20th century — what is it?
Inch: Unit of length. The inch (symbol: in or ″) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.
Awarded a gas-attack Iron Cross in WWI before sharing the 1925 Nobel with Gustav Hertz for the laws of how an electron strikes an atom — who was this German-American physicist?
Hailed as a 'miracle worker' in 1955, this researcher refused to patent his polio vaccine so it could spread worldwide for free — who is he?
Jonas Salk: American inventor of the polio vaccine (1914–1995)
Made from shredded pastry dough layered with cheese and soaked in sugar syrup, this Arab dessert is especially popular during Ramadan, with a famous variant hailing from Nablus — what is it?

One of the five big cats in the genus Panthera, this slender, muscular predator wears dark spots clustered into rosettes and is split today into eight recognised subspecies across Africa and Asia — what is it?
Leopard: Species of cat native to Africa and Asia.

This American stealth strike fighter comes in three flavors — conventional, short-takeoff/vertical-landing, and carrier-based — and with 883 in service is the world's fourth-most-numerous military aircraft. What is it?

Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II: American stealth multirole fighter aircraft. The Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
With the formula MgCl2, this colorless salt forms hydrates and serves as the principal precursor to large-scale production of its namesake metal — what is it?
Magnesium chloride: Inorganic salt: MgCl2 and its hydrates. It forms hydrates MgCl2·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 12.
Widely brewed as a calming herbal tea despite limited clinical evidence for its effects, this annual plant in the daisy family goes by the nickname 'scented mayweed' — which plant?
Matricaria chamomilla: Species of flowering plant.
First isolated in 1921 and encoded by the codon AUG, this essential amino acid also serves as the precursor to cysteine — which amino acid is this?
Native to Southeast Asia, this evergreen tree's leaves are known as kratom, containing alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors — which species?
Mitragyna speciosa: Species of plant. It is under preliminary research for possible antipsychotic and antidepressant properties.

Named for being quieter than its relatives, this large white waterfowl carries an orange beak topped with a black knob that's bigger in males, and is more common in North America than in its native Europe — which bird?
Mute swan: Large species of waterfowl. The mute swan (Cygnus olor) is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order.
Also known in everyday speech as 'brain surgery,' this medical specialty treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and the entire nervous system — what is it called?
Neurosurgery: Medical specialty of disorders which affect any portion of the nervous system.
This medical condition, defined by a body mass index over 30, is linked to heart disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea — what is it?
Obesity: Medical condition of excess body fat.
This paired female gonad releases egg cells and secretes hormones that regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility — which organ?
Ovary: Female reproductive organ that produces egg cells.
One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory and famously preferred cracking open problems to building grand theories — who was he?
Found naturally in mammals' milk and a direct precursor to phenethylamine, this is one of nine amino acids your body can't make, so you eat it in meat, eggs, and legumes — which one?
This egg-laying Australian mammal hunts with its eyes, ears, and nostrils shut, sensing prey by electrolocation — and, oddly for a mammal, it's also venomous. What is it?
Platypus: Species of mammal. Like other monotremes, the platypus has a sense of electrolocation, which it uses to detect prey in water while its eyes, ears and nostrils are closed.
This New World family within the order Carnivora encompasses raccoons, ringtails, coatis, and kinkajous, most of them omnivorous — what family is it?
Procyonidae: Family of mammals. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Native to southern China, this pear tree's fruit goes by dozens of names worldwide - Asian pear, apple pear, nashi pear - but is rarely baked into pies due to its high water content - which species?
Pyrus pyrifolia: Species of pear with round crisp grainy fruit.
Rooted in Minangkabau cooking at the crossroads of the Malacca Strait, this dish slow-cooks meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — what is it?
The second woman ever to win the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine — and the first American-born one — this physicist shared the 1977 award for developing the radioimmunoassay. Who was she?
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow: American medical physicist (1921–2011)

First used in English in the early 15th century and possibly named after a Mediterranean island, this term covers small oily forage fish under 15 centimeters, with larger ones called pilchards — what's the fish?
Sardine: Common name for various small, oily forage fish.
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
Known for a synchronized aerial swarming display called murmuration, this glossy-plumed bird family includes talkative mynas as members — which birds?
Starling: Family of birds. The Sturnidae are named for the genus Sturnus, which in turn comes from the Latin word for starling, sturnus.
This South African biologist made a tiny roundworm, C. elegans, the model organism for studying how bodies develop, sharing a 2002 Nobel for the work — who is he?
Sydney Brenner: South African biologist and Nobel prize winner (1927–2019)
Developed under the codename 'WhiteStar' and unveiled in Hawthorne, California in 2009, this full-size electric sedan won Motor Trend's Car of the Year in 2013 — which car?
Tesla Model S: Battery-electric full-size car. The Tesla Model S is a battery-electric, four-door full-size car that was produced by the American automaker Tesla from 2012 to 2026.
Commonly called jock itch, this contagious fungal infection of the groin and buttocks causes an intensely itchy, red, scaly rash with a well-defined curved border — what is it?
Tinea cruris: Fungal infection. It is often associated with athlete's foot and fungal nail infections, excessive sweating, and sharing of infected towels or sports clothing.
Named after the Turkish word for turban, which it was thought to resemble, this spring-blooming bulb belongs to the lily family and includes about 75 species — which flower?
This abnormal enlargement of veins in the scrotum is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, affecting around 15% of all men — what is it called?
Varicocele: Abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform plexus veins in the scrotum.
With a heart-shaped white facial disc and an eerie screech instead of a hoot, this nocturnal hunter locates small mammals purely by sound — which bird?
Western barn owl: Species of owl. The western barn owl (Tyto alba) is a species of barn owl native to Europe, southwestern Asia, and Africa.
Nicknamed the ZZ plant or eternity plant, this glossy-leaved houseplant genus native to eastern Africa is prized for being nearly impossible to kill — name the genus?
Zamioculcas: Species of plant. Zamioculcas is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, containing the single species Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
Xenon is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for xenon is Xe. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Bismuth is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for bismuth is Bi. Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
